abstract: Alveolar epithelial cell (AEC) inflammation is a key driver of infectious pneumonia pathology. Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) is a central mediator in this response, but its specific regulatory mechanisms at the cellular level remain unclear. TLR4 was identified as a candidate target gene for childhood infectious pneumonia (CIP) using the GeneCards database, and analyzed in a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced A549 AEC injury model. Cell viability, apoptosis, and inflammatory cytokine levels were examined using the cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8) assay, flow cytometry, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) assay, and inflammatory factor detection kits, respectively. Upstream miR-21-5p of TLR4 and its upstream lncRNA OTUD6B-AS1 were predicted using bioinformatics databases, and binding interactions were confirmed by luciferase reporter assays. The functional role of the OTUD6B-AS1-miR-21-5p-TLR4 axis was investigated by transfecting oe-OTUD6B-AS1 and miR-21-5p mimics. LPS upregulated TLR4 in A549 cells. TLR4 knockdown attenuated LPS-induced reductions in viability, cytotoxicity, and apoptosis. Further studies revealed binding of miR-21-5p to both TLR4 and OTUD6B-AS1. OTUD6B-AS1 sponged miR-21-5p to reduce miR-21-5p-mediated repression of TLR4, thereby promoting TLR4 expression and exacerbating the inflammatory response. The OTUD6B-AS1/miR-21-5p/TLR4 axis plays a pivotal role in AEC inflammation and represents a promising therapeutic target for CIP.
